item.title: Passing Functions as Arguments in JavaScript Without Immediate Execution
item.description:
“Passing Functions as Arguments in JavaScript Without Immediate Execution”

A frequent requirement in JavaScript programming involves passing a function as an argument to another function—often termed a “callback”—but ensuring that the passed function is executed only when the receiving function decides to invoke it, not at the moment of the call. Executing the function immediately by using parentheses, like callback(), binds its execution to the initial call site. How can we correctly reference the function instead?

item.title: Python Object Type Determination: type() vs isinstance() vs Alternatives
item.description:
“Python Object Type Determination: type() vs isinstance() vs Alternatives”

When working with dynamic languages like Python, accurately identifying the type of a variable at runtime is a frequent necessity. Several mechanisms exist for this purpose, each carrying different implications regarding inheritance and idiomatic Python style. How do expert developers choose between type(), isinstance(), explicit attribute checks, or adopting abstraction principles?

This exploration details the available tools and established practices for robustly determining an object’s class or abstract nature.

item.title: C++ String Splitting Techniques: Methods and Examples
item.description:
“C++ String Splitting Techniques: Methods and Examples”

Splitting a string into smaller parts based on a delimiter is a common programming task. C++ offers several ways to achieve this, ranging from manual iteration to utilizing powerful libraries. Below are various methods with practical code examples.

Solution 1: Using Boost.Tokenizer

The Boost library provides a robust and flexible tokenizer class that simplifies string splitting.

  • C++11 Version:

    #include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <boost/tokenizer.hpp>

int main() {
    std::string text = "token, test   string";
    boost::char_separator<char> sep(", ");
    boost::tokenizer<boost::char_separator<char>> tokens(text, sep);

    for (const auto& t : tokens) {
        std::cout << t << "." << std::endl;
    }
    return 0;
}

item.title: Python Enum Implementation Options: A Deep Dive
item.description:
“Python Enum Implementation Options: A Deep Dive”

Python’s journey with enumerations has evolved significantly. While earlier versions lacked direct support, the introduction of PEP 435 in Python 3.4 brought built-in enum functionality. Prior to this, and even for more advanced use cases, developers devised several creative methods to simulate enums. This exploration delves into these diverse strategies, offering practical code examples and highlighting their strengths.

Leveraging the enum Module (Python 3.4+)

Python 3.4 and later versions natively support enums through the enum module, primarily defined by PEP 435 . This is the recommended approach for modern Python development.

item.title: Python String Splitting: Efficiently Chunking Text
item.description:
“Python String Splitting: Efficiently Chunking Text”

When working with strings in Python, you often need to break them down into smaller, manageable pieces of a fixed size. This is commonly referred to as “chunking” or “segmenting” a string. Python offers a variety of methods to achieve this, each with its own advantages. Let’s examine several effective approaches.

Solution 1: List Comprehension with Slicing

A concise and Pythonic way to achieve this is by using a list comprehension combined with string slicing. This method iterates through the string with a specified step size and extracts substrings of the desired length.
